records.title: AI for science: testing whether a tool improves research
records.overview: The inherited evidence shows public research priorities, access to AI research resources and a completed evaluation pilot. It does not yet establish that the linked systems consistently improve scientific discovery, replication or research quality in named working laboratories.

sections.heading: Start with a scientific task
paragraphs: AI for science is useful to assess at the level of a task: a particular workflow, institution, dataset and decision. Counting tools or allocating more computing resources does not tell us whether the task improved. A baseline is a documented starting method against which a new method can be compared. It should describe time, cost, data quality, expert effort and the accuracy or reproducibility required for that scientific purpose.

sections.heading: What is established here
paragraphs: Federal priorities and the national research-resource pilot show direction and access infrastructure. NIST's ARIA pilot provides an example of organized evaluation practice. Metrology work concerns how measurements and tests are defined and trusted. NASA use-case records describe reported applications. Together these identify programs, their purposes and the evaluation environment. A completed pilot can demonstrate that a test was run without establishing that its method has delivered durable benefits in every scientific setting.

sections.heading: The steps between demonstration and use
paragraphs: A promising demonstration still needs suitable data, permission to use it, computing access, an evaluation protocol and institutional approval. The laboratory must decide what result is good enough, when an expert should override the system and what happens after a failure. These are practical delivery questions. They also help distinguish a tool available to researchers from one accepted into a specific workflow. Evidence about infrastructure belongs beside the workflow record, with each retaining its own limits.

sections.heading: How a useful comparison works
paragraphs: Compare the AI-assisted method with a prior method or a suitable control on a stable task. Count human checking, failed runs and the resources needed to correct errors. Keep the dataset, model version and evaluation rules visible. A faster output is not automatically a better scientific result if reliability or replication declines. Repeated use across research cycles is more informative than a single favorable demonstration, especially when the record includes overrides, incidents and model changes.

sections.heading: Questions that expose the gap
paragraphs: Which scientific decision did the system help make? Was the result independently checked or reproduced? Did researchers actually use the tool after the pilot? Were excluded tasks and unsuccessful cases recorded? Did computing and labor costs change together? These questions avoid treating access counts as scientific benefit. They also show why claims about discovery speed, experimental yield and research quality need their own measures instead of one broad label such as active use.

sections.heading: The next useful record

They help locate people, facilities and projects, but membership is not a production credential. MEP network results add reported business effects, with attribution to participating clients. Those results should retain their survey basis and separate sales, savings, investment and employment. Census establishment data offers a different statistical perspective; the ASM-to-AIES transition requires a documented bridge before a reader treats successive releases as a continuous manufacturing trend.

sections.heading: Qualification is a customer-facing requirement
paragraphs: For a production claim, useful evidence includes the approved process revision, inspection criteria, lot identity, yield definition and receiving customer's acceptance. Throughput alone leaves an important ambiguity: more units can include rejects or unfinished work. A defensible account separates units started, first-pass conforming units, rework, scrap and accepted shipments. It also records product mix and equipment downtime. These are proposed reporting fields, not observations supplied by the chapter. Their purpose is to make subsequent factory evidence interpretable rather than to prescribe one universal manufacturing metric.

sections.heading: Workforce and facilities need a joined chronology
paragraphs: A training academy can establish that instruction was delivered without establishing that graduates filled a particular employer's vacancies. Track enrollment, completion, credentials, placement and retention as separate cohorts, including the follow-up window. Similarly, an equipment installation should connect to commissioning and qualified operators before it supports a production-readiness statement. The useful local question is whether the right capabilities are available when a facility needs them. Answering it requires employer and training-provider records with compatible dates, not a regional announcement total.

sections.heading: What a stronger next edition would add
paragraphs: The next decisive contribution would be a small set of named establishment histories linking an initial intervention to later accepted output. Each history should show a baseline period, process changes, measurement rules, customer acceptance and a subsequent period with the same definitions. Changes in demand, ownership, staffing and product mix should remain visible as alternative explanations. Readers could then distinguish a promising demonstration, a sustained operating improvement and a broader economic claim without ranking companies whose evidence was collected for different purposes. The goal is a usable account of production, not a larger collection of factory headlines. That distinction should remain visible in every future update.

records.title: Agriculture and Bioeconomy: following research into fields and livelihoods
records.overview: Agricultural progress has to survive a sequence of different tests: a research idea must produce usable material, perform in relevant growing conditions, pass applicable review, reach producers and remain worthwhile under actual management. The September source shelf covers breeding programs, crop reporting, supply-and-demand estimates and plant-trait assessment rules. Together these explain the setting for innovation. They do not yet form a farm-level account of adoption, yield, water demand or household benefit.

sections.heading: Separate a research program from a field result
paragraphs: NIFA's breeding and genomics materials identify supported scientific questions and funded projects. A useful follow-up names the crop, trait, research team and intended environment, then follows the work into datasets, germplasm, replicated trials and any cultivar release. The intervention being evaluated must remain recognizable. A trait studied under controlled conditions should not silently become a claim about commercial farms. Field performance requires the actual treatment, comparator, location, season and management regime, with unsuccessful or inconclusive observations retained alongside promising results.

sections.heading: Regulatory assessment answers a defined question
paragraphs: The CFIA plant-trait directive supplies environmental assessment criteria and applicant responsibilities. Its existence does not authorize an individual product, and an environmental decision does not establish food approval, seed distribution or profitable use. Readers should trace the specific product and jurisdiction through the relevant decision documents. This matters particularly when a research announcement describes a broad technology while the approval concerns a narrower trait or use. The report should explain that scope in ordinary language before discussing commercialization or regional implications.

sections.heading: Use crop reports as context, with their uncertainty intact
paragraphs: Crop Progress and WASDE serve different purposes. Progress and condition reports describe aggregate survey estimates over their stated reporting windows. WASDE provides evolving estimates and forecasts for commodity supply, use, trade and related balances. Revisions can reflect incoming information rather than a sudden change in underlying conditions. Neither product identifies the effect of a particular seed or technology on one farm. A chapter using both should retain issue dates, observation periods and geographic coverage rather than blending weekly conditions with a final harvest result.

sections.heading: Adoption needs an eligible population and an economic account
paragraphs: For a named agricultural innovation, the adoption denominator might be eligible farms, planted area or participating producers; those units answer different questions. The numerator should describe actual use during a defined season, not seed availability or expressions of interest. Understanding why adoption persists also requires attention to input requirements, labor, equipment, market access and producer costs. These factors are analytical questions here, not established explanations. Regional averages should be supplemented by subgroup and farm-type context so that a reported gain does not conceal who could realistically participate.

sections.heading: Build the next field-outcome chain
paragraphs: The most useful addition would pair a named research project with a documented trial and a later producer cohort. The record should preserve weather, irrigation, soil context, pest management and the measurement method, then show which conclusions can travel beyond the original site. Yield, water use, resilience and income should be reported separately. A result can improve one measure while leaving another unresolved. Readers would gain a clear view of what has been demonstrated, the conditions under which it was demonstrated, and the particular field or market evidence needed before treating it as a broadly deployable improvement.

records.title: AI for Science: from model output to reproduced work
records.overview: AI for science is most useful to readers when it is described as part of a research workflow. The model may help select a candidate, interpret a measurement or control a search, but the scientific claim depends on what happens next. The inherited evidence shelf connects measurement resources and evaluation programs to institutional AI records. It supports a careful account of methods and governance while leaving reproduced discoveries and sustained mission benefits to more specific evidence.

sections.heading: Locate the claim within the experiment
paragraphs: Start by identifying what the model actually contributes. Predicting a material property, prioritizing laboratory tests and summarizing documents involve different error consequences. A model score becomes scientific evidence only through an appropriate relationship to observations, experimental controls and the intended question. The report should distinguish training data, evaluation data and newly collected measurements. It should also explain what the model was allowed to see. Without those details, apparent progress may be difficult to separate from reuse of information already present in the research process.

sections.heading: Evaluation resources are a starting point
paragraphs: NIST's AI Metrology Center and TEVV program organize measurement methods and evaluation work. They help researchers choose tests, but they are not blanket endorsements of a model or application. The ARIA pilot adds a bounded example of evaluating systems at multiple levels. Its organizational and application scope remains attached to the result. Readers should look for a named evaluation protocol, tested version, participants and context, then ask whether the same conditions apply to the scientific workflow being discussed. A general assurance label cannot replace that comparison.

sections.heading: Reproduction must include the surrounding workflow
paragraphs: A useful reproduction package describes the dataset version, preprocessing, model configuration, evaluation procedure and relevant instrument settings. It should record which steps required expert judgment and whether unsuccessful runs were excluded. Repeating a computational result is only one part of the chain when the claim concerns physical or biological behavior. The next step may require independent synthesis, a separate instrument or a different laboratory. Those are proposed evidence requirements; this chapter does not assert that the listed programs have completed them for a particular discovery.

sections.heading: Institutional use creates a second set of questions
paragraphs: An organization can list an active AI use case without supplying measures of accuracy, availability, cost or mission benefit. For scientific operations, the responsible institution should identify authorization, access controls, monitoring and the process for handling unexpected behavior. Human review needs a defined role: who may reject a result, change a protocol or suspend use? A workflow that changes after deployment also needs versioned evaluation. These questions connect scientific reliability to operational responsibility while avoiding the assumption that adoption itself demonstrates benefit or safety.

sections.heading: Publish evidence that helps another researcher decide
paragraphs: The next content priority is a set of research histories in which a model-assisted proposal can be followed into an inspectable experiment and a reproduced result. Each should explain the baseline workflow, the AI contribution, verification steps and remaining uncertainties. Time saved, experimental cost and scientific quality should remain separate measures, with the resources used to obtain them visible. Where an independent comparison is unavailable, the report can still describe the demonstrated workflow and its limits. That is a useful contribution for researchers deciding which method to investigate, even before broader productivity or discovery claims become supportable.

records.title: Aviation: connecting aircraft development to dependable service
records.overview: Aviation brings technical development into contact with several independent permissions and operating responsibilities. The September edition covers powered-lift operating rules, integration-pilot selections, an attributed conforming-aircraft milestone and established aviation reporting sources. These are meaningful records, but each answers a limited question. A reader assessing a proposed service needs to know which aircraft, operator, location and activity the evidence concerns, and what remains before passengers or other users can depend on it.

sections.heading: Read the approval stack in parts
paragraphs: Aircraft design approval, production approval, pilot qualification and an operator's authority are distinct objects. The FAA powered-lift rule creates operating and certification pathways within its scope; it does not issue every approval needed by a particular service. Local facilities, airspace procedures and emergency arrangements introduce additional responsibilities. A clear project account should name the relevant authority beside each step and identify the actual document, including conditions. This allows a reader to see where a technical milestone fits without inferring that one approval completes the entire operating chain.

sections.heading: Integration pilots are evidence opportunities
paragraphs: The FAA eIPP selections identify proposed integration work. Selection can make a future test program concrete, but it does not establish completed flights, signed operating arrangements or results. Follow-up reporting should identify the selected partners, intended use, test location and observation plan. The strongest public return would describe what was attempted, the operating conditions and the criteria used to judge it. Unsuccessful tests, limitations and changes to the plan belong in that account. A pilot becomes informative through documented learning, not simply through the prestige of selection.

sections.heading: Keep company milestones attributed
paragraphs: A manufacturer is a primary source for its own announcement, but the company and regulator speak with different authority. The Joby conforming-aircraft record therefore remains an attributed description of a development and test milestone. Readers should look for the corresponding regulator record when the question becomes certification. The same discipline applies to promised range, charging time, maintenance demand or production scale: distinguish a design specification, a test result and a recurring operating measure. Each should retain aircraft configuration and test conditions before comparison with another program.

sections.heading: Service quality depends on the full journey
paragraphs: An aviation service can be technically capable while its usefulness depends on weather, site access, turnaround, charging, staffing and cancellations. These are candidate operating dimensions, not findings about any named operator in this chapter. A measured service account would show scheduled and completed activity, passengers or payload carried, delays, disruptions and the observation window. Accessibility, noise and community impacts require their own affected populations and measurement methods. Comparing a new service with established transport also requires a shared journey definition rather than a single favorable segment of the trip.

sections.heading: The next decisive reporting package
paragraphs: A stronger edition would follow one named pilot or operator from its approved test conditions into repeated flights and a published operating review. The package should identify aircraft, sites, routes, dates, exposure, incidents and corrective actions, with the limits of public disclosure stated. Established airline reporting can offer useful examples of denominator discipline, but its definitions should not be transplanted automatically to a different aviation model. Readers need an account of the service actually demonstrated and the unresolved conditions for expansion. That would make aviation coverage useful to planners, researchers and communities without turning an early milestone into a promise of dependable transport.

records.title: Chips and Compute: the infrastructure behind usable capacity
records.overview: Chips and compute are often described through large investment announcements and projected demand. sections.heading: Follow electricity from forecast to customer service

sections.heading: Permits reveal responsibilities, not completed operation

sections.heading: Supply chains and skills need evidence of delivery

For compute, workload and service definitions would need to accompany utilization claims; for chips, accepted production would need the relevant qualification basis. This would let readers evaluate what capacity has actually become usable and which dependencies remain unresolved, while keeping the wider industrial ambition in view.

records.title: Climate: connecting broad observations to local decisions
records.overview: Climate information becomes useful for infrastructure when a reader can follow it from a defined observation or forecast to a named exposure and a responsible decision-maker. The inherited September shelf spans global climate indicators, seasonal outlooks, station observations, event reports and emissions accounting. These sources describe different parts of the system. Their value comes from using each at its proper scale, then building an explicit bridge to the asset, community or intervention under discussion.

sections.heading: Keep observation, forecast and scenario distinct
paragraphs: NOAA's global reporting describes broad conditions over stated periods, while ENSO discussions provide probabilistic outlooks. Historical station observations answer a more local question, but station moves, missing values and quality flags can affect interpretation. A forecast issued on one date is not an observation of what later happened. A useful account should identify which kind of product it uses, when the information was available and the period it describes. This makes it possible to evaluate the decision without granting its authors knowledge they did not have at the time.

sections.heading: Translate hazards into an asset-specific exposure
paragraphs: The transportation chapter of the National Climate Assessment supplies a broad framework for climate-related infrastructure concerns. Applying it to a bridge, railway, airport or road requires local geography, design, condition and operating information. Exposure is not the same as damage, and damage is not the same as service interruption. Readers should be shown the connecting evidence: the hazard experienced, the component affected, the inspection or operating record and the consequences for users. The chapter proposes this chain without asserting that a particular local loss has been attributed to climate change.

sections.heading: Treat event and loss records as bounded observations
paragraphs: NOAA Storm Events can identify reported events and associated information, but its fields are not a complete account of every local loss. Reporting practices, revisions and coverage matter. An apparent difference between places may reflect reporting as well as physical exposure. A careful comparison retains the source's geographic unit and definition of damage, then checks whether affected assets and periods align. Insurance claims, public repair expenditure and business interruption would add different perspectives; they should not be summed without checking overlap and the type of loss each records.

sections.heading: Emissions accounts require their own boundaries
paragraphs: EPA's national inventory and facility reporting program are complementary rather than interchangeable. Facility thresholds, covered activities, reporting years and estimation methods determine what each can say. A change in reported emissions could coincide with changes in production, ownership, reporting coverage or calculation methods. Readers need those qualifications before interpreting the direction of a series. The useful next question is which activities and gases the comparison includes, and whether the same boundary is maintained over time. A facility series alone cannot establish a complete regional balance or attribute a change to one policy.

sections.heading: Show adaptation as a documented decision and follow-up
paragraphs: The next edition should follow a small number of named adaptation decisions into design, funding, implementation and later operation. A maintenance change and a major capital project would each need a clear objective, baseline condition and measure of service under relevant conditions. Avoided loss is especially demanding because it concerns what might otherwise have happened. Where that comparison is unavailable, the report can still document the intervention, its tested capability and subsequent observations. This gives planners practical evidence while preserving the difference between an adopted response, demonstrated performance and a claim about resilience or avoided harm.

records.title: Critical Minerals: from a resource opportunity to accepted material
records.overview: A mineral resource becomes useful to an industrial customer only after a long chain of technical, commercial and public decisions. The September edition follows national mineral context alongside project permits, financing and industrial support. This helps distinguish the promise of a deposit from the availability of material with the right specification. sections.heading: Begin with the material and its intended use
paragraphs: A discussion of critical minerals should identify the commodity, material form and customer requirement. A mineral occurrence, an estimated resource, a mine product and a qualified processed input are different objects. Substitution may be possible in one use but difficult in another; the report should ask for application-specific evidence rather than assume a universal constraint. USGS commodity summaries provide production, trade and resource context, but their annual cadence and revisions remain relevant when readers compare them with fast-moving project or policy announcements.

sections.heading: Financing changes a project's options

An award record likewise needs distinctions among authorized support, obligations, outlays and realized work. A project profile should retain these financial events in its chronology while showing the next physical and contractual evidence required. This gives readers a useful account of progress without converting the face value of support into production capacity.

sections.heading: Permits and conditions belong to specific jurisdictions

A readable case history should explain who is responsible for demonstrating compliance and which document records acceptance of that demonstration. It should also retain amendments and contested questions where present in the inherited record. A permit creates a defined permission or obligation; it does not prove that every downstream dependency is satisfied or that operation will occur on the originally announced timetable.

sections.heading: Qualification connects extraction to manufacturing

Pilot material, a first accepted lot and recurring supply should remain distinguishable. The proposed reporting chain also includes feedstock sourcing, processing yield, residues and inventory, with units and measurement boundaries explicit. Those fields would help identify where material is being transformed and accepted; they are not measured outcomes established for the projects in this chapter.

It should record changes in product mix, feedstock and ownership before explaining a trend. Supply continuity, cost, environmental performance and customer concentration remain separate questions. Recycling and alternative sources can broaden the account where evidence supports the same material specification. Readers would then see which parts of an industrial supply chain have become dependable and where a resource, financial or permitting milestone still needs a concrete operating return.

records.title: Cybersecurity: making obligations observable in operating systems
records.overview: Cybersecurity coverage becomes useful when it connects a threat or requirement to an organization's actual systems, responsible owners and verified response. The September shelf includes vulnerability metadata, known exploitation, advisories, asset-visibility obligations and post-quantum migration guidance. These are important inputs to prioritization. They do not, on their own, establish local exposure, completed remediation or reduced harm. The report's task is to show how an institution can demonstrate what it has done and what remains uncertain.

sections.heading: A vulnerability record needs an asset context
paragraphs: NVD describes vulnerabilities, while CISA's KEV catalog identifies vulnerabilities known to have been exploited. Neither substitutes for knowing which products and versions an organization operates, where they are reachable and what mitigations are in place. A useful operational account joins the vulnerability identifier to an asset inventory and a responsible owner. It should distinguish an affected product in principle from an exposed installation in practice. This provides a defensible basis for explaining priority without turning a catalog listing into a claim that a named organization has been compromised.

sections.heading: Inventory quality shapes every later measure
paragraphs: Asset visibility is an operating process, not a one-time list. Systems appear, change owners, become disconnected or remain outside routine scanning. A remediation percentage is hard to interpret if its denominator omits important assets. Readers should ask how the inventory was assembled, which environments were covered, when discovery occurred and how exceptions were handled. The same questions apply to cloud services and third-party components. These are proposed reporting dimensions rather than an assessment of any specific agency's coverage in this chapter.

sections.heading: Separate action from verification
paragraphs: A patch deployment log can show that an action was attempted; a later test can show whether the affected condition was resolved. An exception record may document a deliberate temporary mitigation without completing remediation. Incident response similarly moves through detection, containment, investigation, recovery and follow-up, with different evidence at each point. The strongest public account identifies the tested condition, timing, scope and responsible reviewer while protecting sensitive details. It need not reveal exploitable configurations to explain how a conclusion was reached and which systems remain outside the assurance boundary.

sections.heading: Post-quantum migration illustrates the implementation problem
paragraphs: NIST standards and federal migration guidance make cryptographic change more concrete, but a standard does not replace cryptography in an operating system. Institutions need to identify where vulnerable algorithms are used, which information needs long protection and which suppliers control implementation. Procurement, interoperability testing, cutover and retirement then become distinct milestones. The report should keep those records tied to named systems and versions. A plan can be useful evidence of preparation while the actual migration remains unproven; an isolated pilot cannot establish organization-wide completion.

sections.heading: Measure outcomes without rewarding incomplete visibility
paragraphs: Fewer reported incidents might reflect better prevention, but could also reflect detection or reporting differences. A meaningful comparison requires stable incident definitions, exposure and observation windows, with changes in monitoring acknowledged. Time-to-remediate and recovery measures need similar care around starting points and excluded cases. The next edition should favor a small number of transparent institutional histories over an aggregate security score. Readers would gain an account of the obligation, the implementation, the verification and the remaining exposure, supported by records that can be inspected without presenting catalog counts as a substitute for operational assurance.

records.title: Discovery Technologies: turning observations into usable knowledge
records.overview: Discovery technologies expand what can be observed, measured and explored. Their public value depends on more than collecting data: users must understand the instrument, processing, coverage and uncertainty, then apply the result to a defined question. The September shelf spans elevation, satellite imagery, Earth-observation metadata and ocean exploration. It provides a useful map of scientific infrastructure while preserving the distinction between a dataset being available and a decision being improved by its use.

sections.heading: Identify the actual data product
paragraphs: A portal is a route to evidence rather than the evidence object itself. NASA's Common Metadata Repository helps locate collections and granules, but a claim requires the selected dataset, instrument, processing level and version. Elevation and imagery products likewise vary in resolution, coverage and vintage. Readers should be able to identify the exact product behind a map or analysis and understand what was measured directly versus inferred during processing. This basic discipline makes later comparison, correction and reproduction possible.

sections.heading: Coverage determines what can be seen
paragraphs: A data product's apparent completeness can conceal uneven sampling. Cloud cover, survey tracks, revisit timing and instrument limitations affect what observations are available. For elevation, the acquisition date and quality level matter to interpretations of infrastructure or terrain change. For ocean exploration, expedition location and sampling method constrain what can be generalized. A useful account describes the actual observation footprint, not just the broad region associated with a program. Missing or unobserved areas should remain visible rather than be treated as evidence that nothing relevant is present.

sections.heading: Validation connects a signal to an interpretation
paragraphs: An apparent change in imagery or sensor output needs an appropriate comparison and, where possible, independent observations. Processing changes can alter a time series even when the physical system has not changed in the same way. Validation should therefore identify the reference measurements, their timing and their own limitations. The report can explain what level of interpretation has been supported without assigning a universal accuracy label. These are analytical requirements for a future case study, not a claim that all products on the inherited shelf have been validated for every possible local use.

sections.heading: Institutional adoption is an observable step
paragraphs: A planning office, utility or research team may use a dataset in a particular decision. The useful evidence is the decision record or documented workflow that identifies the product, purpose and interpretation. A public download count would not show whether the information changed a decision. A model improvement would not automatically show better outcomes for residents or infrastructure. The chapter should follow adoption into a named process, explaining the role of expert judgment and the alternatives available. That produces a practical account of use without overstating downstream impact.

sections.heading: The next reporting package should be reproducible

It would preserve the selected files, processing steps, validation records and decision date, with enough explanation for another reader to understand the chain. Where the analysis cannot be reproduced publicly, the reason and available verification should be stated. The report should also show whether a later dataset revision changes the interpretation. This approach turns discovery coverage into a resource for users choosing data and methods, while leaving claims about avoided loss, productivity or scientific importance to the evidence needed for those separate questions.

records.title: Energy: from installed equipment to service when it is needed
records.overview: Energy is a receiving system for many of the project's frontier topics. Factories, computing, transport and water infrastructure all depend on electricity that is available at the relevant place and time. sections.heading: Use the right measure for the question
paragraphs: Power capacity describes a rate, while energy describes an amount over time. For storage, duration, state of charge and operating constraints affect what an installation can provide. A nameplate value therefore cannot establish availability or grid value. EIA data can help identify plants and reported activity, but readers must retain the relevant survey, reporting period and revisions. A monthly total answers a different question from interval dispatch during a system event. The report should explain this difference before comparing assets or drawing conclusions about dependable service.

sections.heading: Connect system forecasts to actual projects
paragraphs: Broad electricity-demand analysis can frame the scale of an issue, especially around data centers and industrial expansion. It cannot establish a particular customer's service date or available capacity. Named projects require utility territory, interconnection, tariff and infrastructure records. A regulatory approval can be conditional, and construction can precede energization or customer use. The practical reporting task is to follow each transition with the appropriate document. Readers then see where a regional outlook has become a local engineering and investment decision, and where uncertainty remains.

sections.heading: Storage performs several different jobs
paragraphs: Battery projects can be discussed in terms of energy shifting, frequency response, network support or other services, but those functions should not be collapsed into a single performance score. A documented response to one disturbance is useful evidence for that event. It does not establish annual availability, degradation, revenues or customer savings. A comparable operating account should name the service, required response, actual observation and relevant exposure. sections.heading: Safety and recovery have a chronology

Readers should not let a site name erase generator identities or assume that a corrective-action statement is independently verified closure. The next evidence may be an inspection, a regulator decision or a later operating observation. Safety questions also need the relevant exposure and time window before comparisons. Claims about reduced bills or improved reliability require evidence at the customer level and a defensible comparison; an asset's output is not enough. Public decisions about infrastructure benefit from seeing the accepted service, the costs borne by different parties and the uncertainty that remains. This creates a practical bridge between frontier demand and the electricity system expected to serve it.

sections.heading: Keep dates and stages separate
paragraphs: Publication date, event date, observation period and the date a researcher checked a source each answer a different question. The report preserves them so a later retrieval does not become an earlier observation. Its evidence grammar distinguishes planning, funding, authorization, implementation, acceptance, operation and public outcomes. These are analytical categories, not a promise that every project follows an identical sequence. Some steps run in parallel; others depend on formal conditions. A chapter should show the actual documented relationship rather than force a project into a generic progress ladder.

sections.heading: Admit a measure only within its definition
paragraphs: A numerical observation needs its unit, denominator, geography, period, method and revision lineage. An EIA nameplate-capacity record cannot establish availability; a queue entry cannot establish a completed plant. NERC planning submissions and LBNL scenarios have their own forward-looking meanings. These inherited examples show why the label on a quantity matters as much as the quantity itself. Missing outcome fields remain missing. A calculated value should be added only when the inputs describe compatible objects and the calculation preserves their limitations.

sections.heading: Distinguish description from explanation
paragraphs: A chronology can show that an event preceded another event. It does not establish that the first caused the second. A before-and-after account should retain changes in demand, ownership, measurement or operating context as possible alternative explanations. Comparisons also require compatible populations and definitions before interpretation. Where that standard is not met, the report can still describe each case and explain the mismatch. It should not resolve the problem by assigning a composite score or presenting unlike observations as a league table.

sections.heading: How to use the report
paragraphs: Read the chapter for the question and the relationship, then use the linked source and method resources to inspect the underlying scope. Treat a proposed next artifact as a research requirement, not as evidence that the artifact has already appeared. The authored date records this editorial work; the inherited cutoff remains September 1. Independent subject review is still pending for these reader assets. A source correction or later decision belongs in a dated continuation, preserving the earlier edition so readers can understand what changed and why.

records.title: Source catalogue: follow the issuer, artifact and revision
records.overview: The source catalogue makes the report auditable by connecting readable chapters to stable source identities. A source entry is more than a link: it records who produced the material, what kind of evidence it contains and the limits on using it. The catalogue does not automatically admit every statement found at a URL or turn a newly reachable page into a verified outcome.

sections.heading: Separate a source family from an exact artifact
paragraphs: An agency portal can lead to many datasets, notices and reports. The supporting object for a claim is the selected document, table, file or decision, with its version and scope. A broad source entry can aid discovery, but readers should still be able to identify the exact material used. This is particularly important for rolling pages whose content changes without a new URL. A stable identifier preserves the editorial relationship; it does not guarantee that the remote page will always display the same evidence.

sections.heading: Record the role each source plays
paragraphs: Primary does not mean interchangeable. A company announcement is primary evidence of what the company announced. A regulatory decision has authority within its legal and institutional scope. A statistical release estimates a defined population using a stated method. An oversight report evaluates the work and period it reviewed. The report should state these roles plainly. Government hosting does not automatically turn operator-authored material into an independent audit, and an official planning document does not become an observed operating result.

sections.heading: Preserve revisions and retrieval dates
paragraphs: A changed table or document needs a relationship to its prior version. The catalogue should retain the original locator and identify what was revised, superseded or withdrawn, with dates where available. A checked date means a review occurred on that date; it does not change the observation period. For example, an inherited LBNL queue release still concerns its defined project universe, and an investment announcement remains an announcement even when revisited later. A source-health check can identify a maintenance need, but successful access alone does not revalidate every claim.

sections.heading: Make the route from chapter to evidence visible
paragraphs: Each reader asset carries source IDs drawn from its original Phase 203 record. The focused list identifies the material most relevant to its argument, while the underlying registry retains the wider inherited collection. Method pages and data exports provide additional context for interpreting these links. Readers should be able to determine whether a passage is a source-bound statement, an editorial explanation or a proposal for future research. This prevents a long bibliography from appearing to support claims that no individual source actually establishes.

sections.heading: Handle access limits honestly
paragraphs: Broken links, unavailable files and incomplete extraction should be recorded as access problems rather than proof that an event or artifact does not exist. An official alternative copy may preserve the same document, but its identity and revision need checking. Where access remains limited, the report should narrow its conclusion and specify the next retrieval or review needed. The catalogue's purpose is to preserve a clear chain of responsibility and evidence, including the places where that chain is incomplete, so another reader can evaluate or continue the work.

records.title: Corrections: preserve the old claim and explain the new decision
records.overview: A living reference work needs a correction process that is as inspectable as its evidence. The inherited Phase 201 workflow provides eight stages, from intake through verification and notice. Its purpose is to determine what changed, which claims are affected and how readers should understand the revision. A source refresh can end in No Material Change; it need not produce a factual correction.

sections.heading: Intake and identity resolution
paragraphs: First record the challenged claim, the relevant artifact and when the issue was discovered. Then resolve the entity, issuer, document version and canonical claim identity. These initial steps prevent a correction from being applied to the wrong facility, reporting period or recommendation. A similar title or shared site name is not enough. The prior public statement should remain recoverable while the issue is reviewed, and an unresolved challenge should not silently become a new finding simply because it was submitted.

sections.heading: Source difference and evidence review
paragraphs: The third stage identifies what the source added, removed, revised or superseded. The fourth determines whether that change affects context, an admitted observation, a decision, a project stage or no governed claim. This distinction is practical. A revised forecast does not necessarily alter a previously reported event; a corrected project identity may affect many later interpretations. An inherited capacity announcement, for example, still needs separate operating evidence even if its stated plan changes. Review should focus on the actual changed scope rather than assume every edit has the same significance.

sections.heading: Impact mapping and decision
paragraphs: The fifth stage identifies all dependent sources, signals, dossiers, pathways, panels, reports, exports and updates. The sixth issues the decision with rationale, reviewer, date and receipt. The inherited choices include Correct, Clarify, Retract, Supersede, No Material Change and Bounded Blocker. Each conveys something different to readers. A clarification may improve wording without changing the evidence state; a retraction withdraws a claim. A bounded blocker records the obstacle and next action without fabricating an outcome. The decision should be specific enough to apply consistently wherever the claim appears.

sections.heading: Propagation and verification
paragraphs: The seventh stage applies the decision across affected surfaces while preserving prior versions and independent identities. The eighth checks the result and prepares an appropriate notice when publication is authorized. This includes ensuring that a corrected source statement does not remain contradicted by a summary, export or chart. Same-day events should retain their separate identities. Tests can verify structure and consistency, but they do not replace subject review of the evidence. Repository publication and hosting are also separate actions from preparing the corrected content.

sections.heading: What readers should see
paragraphs: A useful notice states the affected claim, the earlier and revised interpretation, the controlling evidence and whether the change alters a material conclusion. It should distinguish the date of the underlying event from the date of correction. Historical editions remain valuable because they show what information supported an earlier reading. This appendix describes the inherited process; it does not claim that a new correction has been adjudicated for any case. The linked correction resources provide the appropriate place to inspect actual decisions and their continuation history.

records.title: Accessible use and translation: preserve meaning across reading formats
records.overview: An accessible edition should make the same evidence easier to reach and understand without weakening its qualifications. The inherited Phase 202 contracts cover plain-language English, low-bandwidth HTML and human-reviewed French and Spanish. Those contracts specify work to perform; they are not themselves proof of tested accessibility or approved translation. This appendix explains how readers and editors should evaluate the resulting editions.

sections.heading: Plain language must preserve the claim
paragraphs: A plain-language account should lead with the bounded answer, define necessary terms and explain what remains unknown. Simplifying prose should not turn a plan into an outcome or remove the denominator behind a percentage. For example, an investment commitment and a completed facility remain different even when the explanation is shortened. Source and correction links should stay close enough to the discussion that a reader can inspect them. The objective is to reduce unnecessary effort while preserving the distinctions on which a trustworthy interpretation depends.

sections.heading: A low-bandwidth edition needs functional content
paragraphs: The inherited contract calls for semantic HTML, direct source access and a text-first payload target before source downloads. Core information should remain available without a client-rendering dependency. Tables need captions and row headers, meaningful visuals need text alternatives, and color cannot be the sole carrier of meaning. Navigation and reading order should remain intelligible on small screens and with assistive technology. These are acceptance requirements for the edition; listing them does not establish that the rendered pages have already passed device or accessibility testing.

sections.heading: Translation is a reviewed interpretation
paragraphs: French and Spanish editions need to preserve meaning, proper names, source identifiers and evidence states. Technical and institutional terms require particular care because a familiar translation can imply a different legal or administrative concept. The reviewer should compare the translated passage with the canonical English record and its source scope, not merely check fluency. The inherited process requires a translator, a qualified reviewer and a dated approval receipt. Until those decisions occur, a translation remains a draft and should not be presented as a reviewed public edition.

sections.heading: Versions and corrections must travel together
paragraphs: Each alternate edition should identify the canonical content version it follows. If the underlying claim changes, the dependent edition needs review so that readers in different formats do not receive conflicting conclusions. A source limitation, withdrawal or corrected denominator can be more important than the surrounding prose. The change process should therefore track affected translations and reading formats alongside the main chapter. Older editions may remain available as history when clearly labeled, but an unreviewed translation of new text should not inherit an earlier approval automatically.

sections.heading: What this report currently offers
paragraphs: These reader assets provide substantive English editorial drafts with an inherited September 1 cutoff and a September 10 authored date. Their presence does not claim independent subject approval, translated approval or a new tested accessibility certification. The linked resources show the existing reading and method framework, while the Phase 202 contracts describe the requirements for further editions. Readers should be able to choose a format without losing source scope, uncertainty or correction history. That consistency is the substantive goal of accessible publication, alongside the practical usability of the interface.

records.title: Limitations and open research: make the missing evidence specific
records.overview: The report's ambition is to explain frontier systems without hiding where its evidence stops. The inherited edition contains strong source trails but uneven depth across topics, places and operating stages. A null outcome or an open classification records a research boundary. It is not a negative finding about the real world. This appendix explains how those boundaries should guide the next work.

sections.heading: Coverage is not representativeness
paragraphs: A set of well-documented cases can be informative without representing every project or jurisdiction. Public agencies and large organizations may publish more detailed material than smaller or less accessible institutions. English-language discovery can also shape what enters the shelf. The report should describe its selected cases and source reach rather than present the collection as a statistical sample. A topic with more records is not necessarily more advanced. Expanding coverage should target missing systems and perspectives while preserving the same admission standards.

sections.heading: A missing value has a reason
paragraphs: Outcome fields can remain empty because the relevant period has not ended, the public record lacks a compatible denominator, the artifact is inaccessible or no governed review has admitted it. Those reasons are different and should be stated. A planned project in a queue is not an observed failure, and a scenario range is not a realized result. The inherited energy and compute sources illustrate these distinctions. Readers benefit from knowing the exact obstacle, because it determines whether the next step is waiting, retrieval, reconciliation or a new analytical method.

sections.heading: Comparability and attribution remain demanding
paragraphs: Repeated values do not form a valid trend if the population, unit or reporting method changed. Two projects can also use the same word for different stages, such as completion or acceptance. The report should document those mismatches before comparison. Causal explanations require still more evidence, including credible treatment of alternative explanations and the appropriate comparison. Where these conditions are absent, a bounded narrative can remain useful. It should not manufacture certainty through a score, a ranking or a general claim that one system caused a broader public outcome.

sections.heading: Specify the next decisive artifact
paragraphs: An open research entry should name the entity, issuer, required document or observation, scope and trigger for review. For an infrastructure project, the next artifact might be an accepted inspection; for adoption, a fixed-cohort subscriber return; for production, qualified and accepted output over a defined period. The entry should also explain what would remain unresolved after that artifact arrives. This keeps research cumulative. It avoids repeatedly collecting adjacent announcements that add context but cannot answer the particular question holding the claim open.

sections.heading: What completion means for this edition
paragraphs: Completing the report's editorial structure does not complete every external project, future evidence gate or expert review. These drafts deepen the reader-facing explanation of the inherited record without changing those states. A later return belongs in a dated decision and continuation, with affected pages updated through the correction process. The most valuable next work will connect selected open chains to real operating and user outcomes while expanding underrepresented coverage. Readers should be able to see both the substantive account already supported and the concrete evidence needed to make the account more decisive.

records.title: Compute, power, and water
records.overview: A compute campus becomes useful when its machines, utilities and operating organization work together at a named site. Announced computing capacity describes only part of that system. The September 1 evidence baseline contains national demand forecasts, generation connection requests and specific utility decisions. Read together, they explain where an investigation should move from a promising investment to the electricity and water services that sustain it. They do not establish a common readiness score.

sections.heading: Three different meanings of capacity
paragraphs: Computing equipment, electrical service and water supply have different units, owners and operating conditions. A processor inventory does not specify how much power a utility has accepted an obligation to deliver. An electrical connection does not state which cooling configuration is installed, its water demand or whether the relevant water infrastructure has been accepted. The useful analytical approach is to describe each service separately before asking how their operating limits interact.

This makes a project profile more informative than a single campus capacity number. It should identify the facility, equipment configuration, utility connection, operating period and receiving parties. A campus containing several buildings may have different answers for each building. The first operating facility cannot establish the condition of facilities still under construction.

sections.heading: Forecast demand and proposed supply are different populations
paragraphs: NERC's 2025 assessment anticipates summer peak-demand growth exceeding 224 GW between 2025 and 2035. Its underlying planner submissions are forecasts, not measurements of future consumption. The assessment's distinction between approved and prospective supply matters because it exposes different planning commitments. Neither category guarantees that every proposed data center will connect or that every proposed resource will operate when needed.

Berkeley Lab's Queued Up 2026 describes another population: approximately 8,200 active transmission-level requests at the end of 2025. Around 549 GW already had a draft or executed interconnection agreement without commercial operation. These records reveal a connection-to-operation gap. They cannot be subtracted directly from NERC demand projections because geography, timing, resource capability and inclusion rules differ.

sections.heading: Northern Virginia shows the institutional handoffs
paragraphs: The inherited Golden-Mars and GS-5 case contains two concrete decisions. Virginia approved a future large-load rate class, scheduled to become effective January 1, 2027, and conditionally approved a transmission project with a local route dependency. The first concerns the terms under which a class of customers would be served. The second concerns authority for a physical transmission proposal. Their proximity does not make them one customer delivery event.

The next useful questions therefore concern final routing, land rights, construction, inspection and energization, followed by an identifiable customer agreement. Those are distinct documents with different responsible parties. A regulatory approval can resolve an institutional dependency while leaving the physical service dependency open.

sections.heading: Arizona makes the water connection concrete
paragraphs: Phoenix relays TSMC's Fab 1 production and Fab 2 construction-completion claims; a separate official record describes Fab 3's structural milestone. A Phoenix wastewater agreement specifies a project-level infrastructure relationship. That agreement is more specific than a regional water discussion because it names parties and improvements. It still does not document completed conveyance infrastructure, accepted reclaimed-water service or metered performance for each fab.

As analysis, this suggests treating water infrastructure as an operating interface rather than a background resource assumption. The relevant questions are what service crosses the interface, who accepts it and under what conditions. A regional model can frame supply pressure, but it cannot answer a facility water-balance question.

sections.heading: Why the binding constraint can change
paragraphs: During construction, a route decision or equipment delivery may determine the next milestone. During operation, maintenance, operating limits or service interruptions may become more relevant. This is a way to organize evidence, not a finding that a particular constraint caused a particular delay. A project history should retain alternative explanations and the issuer of any attribution.

The relationship also depends on configuration. Storage power alone does not specify duration; a national electricity-use estimate does not allocate demand to a county; and a cooling assumption does not establish an accepted water requirement. Combining these measures without their definitions would create precision while removing the information that determines whether the comparison is meaningful.

sections.heading: What would strengthen the next edition
paragraphs: For Northern Virginia, the decisive additions are the final route or land instrument, accepted transmission assets and a named customer service record. For Arizona, they are facility-specific utility acceptance and operating measurements. Repeated reporting should retain the same building or fab identity, measurement period, units, configuration and exception treatment so readers can distinguish a new measurement from a changed definition.

The present conclusion is narrower than a capacity forecast: the repository can trace several important handoffs but cannot yet turn them into dependable campus output. An independently reviewed account would connect delivered utilities to recurring operation, explain interruptions and disclose which links remain supported only by plans or issuer statements.

records.title: Mining, processing, and manufacturing
records.overview: A mineral resource, a financed processing plant and an installed battery describe different points in a production system. The September 1 corpus contains evidence at all three levels, but it does not connect them into a verified material flow. The practical task is to follow a named material through extraction, processing, specification, customer acceptance and repeated deliveries. This account explains what the existing records contribute and where apparently impressive capacity numbers stop being comparable.

sections.heading: Begin with the product a customer can accept
paragraphs: A manufacturing customer receives material with a specified composition and acceptable variation, not a national reserve estimate. Starting from the required product helps clarify which upstream records matter. Resource identification, extraction authorization, processing design and material qualification answer different questions. Their units may also differ: ore, contained mineral, refined compound and finished component cannot be treated as interchangeable quantities.

The implication is analytical rather than a claim about any project's chemistry. A usable supply-chain account should state what enters each process, what leaves it, who measures the result and who accepts it. Without those interfaces, adding announced capacities may double-count the same material at successive stages or join facilities that do not actually supply each other.

sections.heading: What the Thacker Pass financing record establishes
paragraphs: DOE's Thacker Pass record fixes a federal loan of approximately $2.26 billion and describes facilities designed for about 40,000 tonnes of battery-grade lithium carbonate annually. It identifies a financing commitment and a proposed product, giving the project more specificity than a general statement about lithium demand. The designed output remains a target in this evidence account.

The record does not by itself establish drawdowns, completed construction, commissioned equipment, qualified product or customer receipts. Financial close can reduce uncertainty about a funding arrangement without resolving those other questions. Reading the distinction correctly allows the financing milestone to remain useful without promoting it into operating production.

sections.heading: Permits define conditions as well as permission
paragraphs: The paired Nevada case also includes Rhyolite Ridge's water-pollution-control permit. Its pre-operation structure includes notice, inspection, modeling, monitoring, reporting and closure conditions. These requirements give investigators a practical sequence of records to seek. They also show why a permit title is not an adequate summary of the project's operating position.

A subsequent inspection or accepted monitoring submission would resolve a different question from the permit itself. Some conditions may apply before operation, others during operation and others at closure. A chronology should therefore attach each condition to its responsible authority and event, rather than compress all requirements into a single label such as permitted or completed.

sections.heading: Battery deployment is downstream context, not a mineral balance
paragraphs: EIA reports 43.6 GW of operational utility-scale battery nameplate capacity at the end of 2025 and an additional 8.3 GW in the first half of 2026. Its Manatee example identifies 409 MW of battery capacity alongside 75 MW of solar capacity. These figures describe electrical infrastructure, not the quantities or origins of lithium compounds used to construct it.

Neither the national additions nor Manatee's power rating can demonstrate that a named mine supplied accepted material. Converting power capacity into material demand would require additional chemistry, duration, design and sourcing information. The source is valuable as evidence of a downstream asset inventory; it cannot close the upstream qualification chain.

sections.heading: Manufacturing commitments need facility-specific interpretation
paragraphs: Commerce's July 2026 TSMC announcement describes an additional $100 billion commitment, taking announced U.S. investment to $265 billion and twelve proposed manufacturing and packaging facilities. This is an investment scope, not twelve operating facilities. The separate Phoenix record provides narrower distinctions among individual fab milestones and a wastewater agreement.

Together the records illustrate how capital ambition and physical delivery coexist. The investment statement can describe intended scale while the city record describes selected facility events. Neither supplies an audited input-output balance, recurring qualified production or a verified link to a particular mineral supplier. Keeping those limits visible prevents the semiconductor example from becoming a generic proof of domestic supply-chain completion.

sections.heading: The evidence needed for recurring supply
paragraphs: A stronger account would join named commissioning tests to product-lot identities, specification results, customer acceptance and shipment records. Repeated periods would then show whether accepted deliveries were sustained, while recording rejected material, rework, inventory changes and interruptions. These are proposed analytical requirements, not assertions that a company has failed to meet them.

The immediate open records differ by case: Nevada needs condition satisfaction, commissioning and qualified-lot evidence; Arizona needs facility-level qualification and recurring output. EIA's operating asset inventory should remain separate from both. The resulting picture would be a traceable production chain whose missing links are explicit, rather than a regional capacity total assembled from incompatible stages.

records.title: Infrastructure, access, and affordability
records.overview: Infrastructure matters to people through the service they can obtain, the terms of access and the burden of paying for it. Those outcomes are not contained automatically in a construction or funding announcement. The inherited evidence spans compute investment, electricity demand, large-load regulation and broadband reporting rules. It supports a practical distinction between available capacity, actual use and affordability, while leaving the household and business outcomes that require compatible observations unresolved.

sections.heading: Follow a service from availability to use
paragraphs: The first question is what service is available to which eligible population. The second is whether people or organizations actually take it. The third is whether the service is reliable and affordable enough to remain useful. Each question needs a different denominator. Eligible addresses are not active subscribers; installed connections are not completed visits; and a tariff is not a household bill.

A reader-facing account should show these stages in ordinary terms. It can describe coverage without claiming adoption, or adoption without claiming affordability. The missing measurements should be specified precisely enough that a later return can change the answer without redefining the original population.

sections.heading: Compute funding does not measure public access
paragraphs: Commerce's July 2026 letters of intent cover seven compute-supply-chain companies and proposed support of up to $874 million. Photonics, memory, packaging and related technologies are represented. The letters identify intended support and technical areas; they do not establish final awards, disbursement, completed production or access to a service by a defined customer group.

Berkeley Lab's data-center study supplies a different scale of context: estimated U.S. electricity consumption of 176 TWh in 2023, with scenario-dependent values for 2028. The scenarios can inform questions about resource demand. They say nothing directly about how the cost is allocated among customers or whether a particular community gains more affordable computing, broadband or electricity.

sections.heading: A tariff decision is one part of the cost story
paragraphs: Virginia's GS-5 decision gives the corpus a concrete large-load rate mechanism, scheduled for January 2027. It is more informative for cost allocation than a national demand scenario because it identifies a regulated customer category. The Golden-Mars decision separately identifies a transmission proposal and local route condition. Neither record establishes a completed customer connection in the inherited baseline.

An affordability account would need the applicable agreement, charges, actual consumption and relevant customer population. It would also need to distinguish direct customer charges from any wider system costs. Those questions cannot be answered by dividing an infrastructure investment announcement by a population or treating future tariff effectiveness as a measured bill change.

sections.heading: Broadband contracts demonstrate the right denominators
paragraphs: Montana's reporting controls distinguish active subscribers from equipment shipped to project locations. Its acceptance framework also separates latency, download and upload performance, and outage time. That is a useful design example: delivery of customer equipment is an input, subscription is a use state, and performance measurements concern the quality of that use.

The existence of those reporting rules does not supply a completed quarter or prove compliant service. They show what an adequate return should contain. For affordability, the next layer would identify recurring price, installation charges, equipment charges, discounts and the period over which customers face them, along with a defensible measure of income or resources if a burden ratio is reported.

sections.heading: Distribution changes the meaning of an average
paragraphs: An average price or average performance figure can describe a population while concealing who is excluded. Analysis should ask whether the population includes all eligible users, only connected users or only respondents. A service may expand geographically while remaining unused by some eligible households. That possibility is a reason to obtain separate evidence, not a conclusion that a particular program has excluded people.

The same care applies to geography. A national computing estimate cannot be allocated to Northern Virginia without a local method. A state broadband requirement cannot describe a particular provider's actual customers without a return. Comparable distribution analysis therefore depends on explicit eligibility, observation dates and subgroup definitions, not simply on having many regional numbers.

sections.heading: Build an account that can answer a resident's question
paragraphs: The useful final product would answer who can obtain the service, who uses it, what they pay, what performance they receive and what changed over a stated period. A clear profile would identify taxes and one-time charges, explain discount eligibility, and disclose which outcomes remain unmeasured. It should preserve price and quality separately rather than combine them into an unexplained value score.

The next decisive evidence is consequently a named service return with a fixed eligible cohort, active-use count, price schedule and measured quality. For the Virginia case, a customer agreement and observed service would come first. Until those links are documented, the present sources support infrastructure and reporting context, not a conclusion about realized affordability.

records.title: Standards, procurement, and implementation
records.overview: A standard becomes operational through choices about scope, purchases, tests, acceptance and ongoing responsibility. Publishing the requirement is a milestone, but it does not complete those choices. This chapter uses the inherited post-quantum procurement case to make the sequence concrete, then contrasts it with water-governance and modeling records. The contrast matters: a technical model, an operating decision and a procurement guide carry different authority even when all influence the same investment discussion.

sections.heading: Identify what kind of document is controlling the claim
paragraphs: A standard specifies a requirement or method within a stated scope. A procurement document assigns work and commercial responsibilities. A model estimates conditions under assumptions. An operating decision authorizes or directs action. Readers need these distinctions before asking whether an institution has implemented a policy; otherwise the existence of any official document can appear to answer a much broader question.

The September 1 source pair includes Reclamation's post-2026 Colorado River framework and the Phoenix groundwater-model update. Neither is evidence that a named organization purchased or deployed a standards-compliant product. Their value here is to show why technical context and public authority must be connected through identifiable implementation records rather than treated as interchangeable evidence.

sections.heading: GSA provides a concrete acquisition bridge
paragraphs: GSA's June 2025 post-quantum buyer's guide maps cryptographic inventory, assessment, transition planning, implementation, maintenance and training to federal acquisition support. This is a meaningful institutional contribution: it translates a broad migration problem into categories of work that an agency can procure. The guide still does not disclose a completed agency inventory or a particular awarded order.

A reader can use the guide to distinguish preparation from execution. Inventory work identifies which systems and dependencies are exposed. An acquisition record identifies what a supplier is obliged to deliver. Test and acceptance records then establish whether the delivered implementation meets the receiving agency's requirements. A contract vehicle alone establishes none of those downstream results.

sections.heading: Acceptance belongs to an exact configuration
paragraphs: The quantum topic's inherited sources distinguish final standards, a backup-algorithm selection and preliminary credential specifications. These are useful but different development states. An algorithm selection should not be described as a final standard, and a draft credential specification should not be described as deployed infrastructure. The implementation question is which version was used, in what system and with what dependent components.

As analysis, a practical acceptance package would tie test results to a named configuration and declared operating conditions. It would record exceptions, interoperability results and the responsible receiver. A successful component test can support that component without establishing that an institution has completed a migration across every application, certificate, device and external connection.

sections.heading: Water decisions show why authority and assumptions must stay separate
paragraphs: Reclamation's framework supplies expected reservoir conditions and an initially expected water-year 2027 release of 6.0–7.0 million acre-feet, subject to adjustment through April. ADWR's Phoenix Version 3 memorandum models unmet demand over a 100-year horizon. These are not two measurements of the same outcome: one concerns reservoir operations and the other a regional groundwater model with its own assumptions and observational basis.

A facility water claim would require a further link to the responsible provider, applicable permissions and actual service. The TSMC wastewater agreement supplies one project-specific instrument, but it still does not establish completed, accepted water infrastructure. This is the same documentary discipline used in procurement: locate the applicable authority, then verify the named implementation and receiving party.

sections.heading: Implementation includes managing the old system
paragraphs: A replacement can be installed while the prior system remains necessary. In a cryptographic migration, the inherited GSA case explicitly leaves tested cutover, operational acceptance and retirement of vulnerable systems unresolved. That distinction makes maintenance and transition evidence part of the main story, rather than a footnote after procurement.

The evidence should show who can authorize cutover, what exceptions remain and how the organization knows its intended configuration is operating. This is a proposed method for evaluating implementation, not a claim that any agency has retained unsafe systems or failed a test. A responsible narrative states the specific unknown rather than converting an incomplete public record into a negative verdict.

sections.heading: The next records that would change the answer
paragraphs: For post-quantum migration, the strongest additions would be a named order, its accepted deliverables, configuration-specific validation, an operational cutover record and evidence of legacy retirement. For water infrastructure, they would be applicable provider instruments, accepted assets and service measurements. Each document should retain its issuer, date, version and scope so later revisions can be interpreted correctly.

The present conclusion is that the corpus explains several pathways from public direction to implementation but does not prove their completion. Progress becomes clearer when the account identifies which handoff has actually occurred. The same method also makes remaining work actionable without pretending that a model, guide, announcement or procurement option is an operating result.
